$comment: Player-facing release notes. Committed and imported at build time, NOT published to R2. See content/README.md for why this differs from info.json.

releases.title: Card names that were missing from the page
releases.summary: Some rules text was leaving out the character it referred to. That text is back, dual-colour cards look right, and the Thai rulings have been redone.

changes.text: Missing character names in ability text, on 24 card pages.
Skill and art names quoted in rules text stayed Japanese. They now match the translation shown on the card itself.
Blurry colour symbol on dual-colour cards. They now show both badges at full size.
Colour filters find dual-colour cards under both of their colours.
An effect that searches card names by keyword quoted the Japanese word, which no card displays.
Thai rulings re-translated. Seventeen answers were showing as Japanese.

releases.title: The list remembers where you were
releases.summary: Closing a card used to drop you back at the top of the list, depending on your screen width. It does not any more. This page and the header also had a tidy up.

changes.text: Opening a card and closing it again sent you back to the top of the list. Whether it happened depended on how wide your window was, which is why it survived a first attempt at fixing it. Escape, the close button and your browser's Back button all keep your place now, at every window size.

This page groups its entries. The coloured labels used to repeat on every line, so a release with eight entries showed eight labels carrying three words between them. Each label now appears once, with its entries underneath.
GitHub and Discord have moved out of the three dots menu and into the header itself, on wide screens. On a phone or a tablet they stay in the menu, along with everything else that was already there.

releases.title: New cards, and a fix behind the scenes
releases.summary: The card set is up to date with the official list, including the new hEB01 set. Card data reaches the site on its own, so you already had these before this note appeared.

changes.text: 96 new cards from the official list, including the hEB01 set, in all seven languages. The Data Status page always shows the current count and when it was last updated.

The site's visitor statistics were not recording anything. They had been switched off in a way that looked like it was working, and had collected nothing since launch. What we collect is described on the About page.

releases.title: The rebuilt wiki
releases.summary: The site has been rebuilt from scratch. Every card now has its own page you can link to, the filters work properly, and it finally behaves on a phone.

changes.text: Every card has its own page. All 2,463 of them, so you can link a card to a friend, bookmark it, or find it from a search engine. The old site had no card pages at all.
Filter by set code. Type a set code like hBP03 into the search box and it becomes a filter, with its own URL you can share.
Tag filters returned nothing. Every tag matched zero cards, in all seven languages: 0期生, every generation, every group. They work now, and 0期生 returns 165 cards.
Searches with lots of results failed. Any search matching more than 100 cards returned an error instead of results.
A rebuilt look. Card names on the grid, a density control for how much fits on screen, and a filter sidebar on wide screens instead of a panel that covered everything.
The phone lost three things. Data status, GitHub and the Discord invite were desktop-only and simply vanished on a narrow screen, with nothing to show they were missing.

Translations that cannot disagree with themselves. All seven languages were re-translated so that two cards printing the same Japanese can no longer come out differently. It is now structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely. Thai also had the cheer resource spelled four different ways in rules text, and it is one spelling now.
A data status page that tells you what the official card list did, not just what our database did. A translation pass on our side no longer looks like new cards being printed.
